```plato

    //==
    // # IPeriodic
    //
    // RESOLVED (was TODO(interface-gap): a wrapping helper needs Modulo on the
    // period type, and Plato was said to have no type-parameter constraint
    // syntax). The premise was false — interface `where` clauses are live and used
    // (IInterval / IBounds in intervals-bounds.concepts.plato, IMetricSpace
    // in algebra.concepts.plato). IPeriodic<TPeriod> now carries
    // `where TPeriod: IAdditive, TPeriod: IModular`, and WrapPhase below is derived
    // from that bound. The one implementor path
    // (IPeriodicCurve<TRange> inherits IPeriodic<Number>) satisfies it: Number
    // implements IReal, which inherits IArithmetic, which inherits both.
    //
    // The old note also claimed the missing Eval was a second blocker. It is not
    // one for WrapPhase, which takes the domain value as a parameter rather than
    // reading it off the surface. It IS what keeps wrapped *evaluation* from being
    // derived here: a generic EvalWrapped needs a receiver that is both IPeriodic
    // and IProcedural, and a library function cannot state a two-interface bound —
    // MethodDeclaration takes no type parameters at all, so a constraint can only
    // sit on an interface declaration. IPeriodicCurve is the interface that has both, and
    // EvalWrapped lives there (curves.library.plato).
    //
    // NormalizedPhase is likewise not derivable generically: dividing a TPeriod by
    // a TPeriod to get a Number needs a division IModular does not supply.

    // Folds a domain value into the half-open interval [0, Period). The extra
    // "+ Period then modulo" corrects the truncated remainder, which is negative
    // for negative t. Precondition: Period > 0.
    WrapPhase(self: IPeriodic<$TPeriod>, t: $TPeriod): $TPeriod
        => ((t % self.Period) + self.Period) % self.Period;
```
